propositions: _ref_lock.py was pinned at exactly 800 lines (the hard module-size cap for src/rebar files) with zero margin for future changes after a two-line bugfix landed

splitting _ref_lock.py requires moving the tail cluster (~92 LOC: CAS-rejection markers, lease-mismatch logic, and push functions) to a sibling _ref_lock_push.py via lazy_load, while keeping wrapper stubs in the parent to preserve call-site identity and test compatibility

the child module must receive the parent as an explicit core argument and read core._git, core._REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS, and core.logger at call time so that monkeypatch.setattr(_ref_lock, '_git', ...) in tests still intercepts mocked dependencies and logging happens on the rebar_reconciler._ref_lock logger

the three call sites in _ref_lock.py that invoke _push_cas and _push_delete_cas (lines 393, 422, 476) must remain byte-identical with no NameError after the split to avoid breaking the remote acquire/release/advance paths

_ref_lock.py must land under 730 LOC (providing 70-line margin under the 800 cap) and _ref_lock_push.py must remain over the 100-LOC floor, with all acceptance criteria verified including test pass, module-size contract, lint, typecheck, and complexity ratchet gates
